events.title: East African Community Treaty
events.summary: The treaty for the establishment of the East African Community was signed on 30 November 1999. It entered into force on 7 July 2000 following its ratification by the original three Partner States – Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania.

events.title: The National Alliance is founded
events.summary: The National Alliance (TNA) was a political party in Kenya. It took on its current identity when Uhuru Kenyatta assumed control and renamed it as the vehicle for his 2012 presidential campaign.

events.title: Kenya Airways Flight 431 crashes
events.summary: Kenya Airways Flight 431 was an international scheduled Abidjan–Lagos–Nairobi passenger service, operated by Kenyan national airline Kenya Airways. On 30 January 2000, the Airbus A310 serving the flight crashed into the sea off the Ivory Coast, shortly after takeoff at night from Félix-Houphouët-Boigny International Airport, Abidjan.

events.title: Kyanguli Fire Tragedy
events.summary: The Kyanguli Fire Tragedy occurred on the night of 25 March 2001 when a dormitory at Kyanguli Secondary School in Machakos District, Kenya, was set on fire in an act of arson by two 16-year-old students of the school. Sixty-seven people died in the incident and another 19 were injured, including one of the perpetrators.

events.title: The East African Legislative Assembly opens
events.summary: The East African Legislative Assembly (EALA) is a sub-organ of the larger East African Community, being the legislative arm of the Community. Members are sworn into five-year terms.

events.title: Kenya Institute Of Security & Criminal Justice is founded
events.summary: The Kenya Institute of Security and Criminal Justice (KISCJ) is a public institution established in 2002 in Nairobi, Kenya.
events.source_name: Wikipedia: Kenya Institute of Security and Criminal Justice

events.title: Kenya National Commission on Human Rights
events.summary: The Kenya National Commission on Human Rights (KNCHR) is an autonomous national human rights institution, established by the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights Act, 2011. It is a successor to the body of the same name established by an earlier Act of Parliament in 2002.
events.source_name: Wikipedia: Kenya National Commission on Human Rights

events.title: National Rainbow Coalition is founded
events.summary: The National Rainbow Coalition (NARC) is a political party in Kenya. As an alliance, it was in power from 2002 and 2005 when it collapsed due to disagreements between members over a constitutional referendum.

events.title: National Environment Management Authority is established
events.summary: The National Environment Management Authority (NEMA) is the Kenyan government agency responsible for the management of the environment and environmental policy. It is a Semi-Autonomous Government Agency (SAGA) within the Ministry of Environment and Forestry.
events.source_name: Wikipedia: National Environment Management Authority of Kenya

events.title: 2002 Kenyan general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Kenya on 27 December 2002. Voters elected the president, members of the National Assembly and local officials.

events.title: Mwai Kibaki becomes president
events.summary: The presidency of Mwai Kibaki began at 11:00 AM GMT on Monday 30 December 2002, when Mwai Kibaki was inaugurated as the 3rd president of Kenya and ended on 9 April 2013 when he handed over to Uhuru Kenyatta. A NARC candidate, Kibaki was a businessman and member of parliament of Othaya constituency prior to his 2002 election victory over KANU nominee Uhuru Kenyatta.

events.title: A tribunal investigates Chief Justice Chunga
events.summary: The Bernard Chunga Tribunal was a tribunal set up to investigate the then Chief Justice Bernard Chunga.

events.title: Kwani? is founded
events.summary: Kwani? (derived from the Sheng slang "so what?") was a prominent Kenyan literary magazine headquartered in Nairobi.

events.title: The Ringera report on the judiciary
events.summary: The 2003 Ringera Judiciary Report was a Kenya Government report published by the Integrity and Anti-Corruption Committee of the Judiciary in Kenya in order to implement a policy known as radical surgery introduced by the new government of President Mwai Kibaki. The committee was led by Justice Aaron Ringera.

events.title: The 9th Parliament opens
events.summary: The 9th Parliament of the Republic of Kenya was opened by elected President Mwai Kibaki on February 18, 2003. It was the first time that the formerly-dominant Kenya African National Union of Daniel arap Moi was in the minority.

events.title: 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake
events.summary: On 26 December 2004, at 07:58:53 local time (UTC+7), a Mw 9.2–9.3 earthquake struck with its epicenter off the west coast of Aceh, in northern Sumatra, Indonesia. The undersea megathrust earthquake, known in the scientific community as the Sumatra–Andaman earthquake, was caused by a rupture along the fault boundary between the Burma plate and the Indian plate, and reached a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX in some areas.
events.source_name: Wikipedia: 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami

events.title: Ishaqbini Hirola Conservancy is established
events.summary: The Ishaqbini Hirola Conservancy is a community-based conservation area located in Garissa County, Kenya. The conservancy covers approximately 72 km2 (28 sq mi).

events.title: Kenya Film Commission
events.summary: The Kenya Film Commission (KFC) was established by the Kenyan government in 2005. It came into full function in mid-2006.

events.title: Madaraka People's Movement
events.summary: The Madaraka People's Movement, formerly known as Madaraka Party of Kenya, is a political party in Kenya which identifies itself as "youth-focused". Formed in June 2005, Madaraka Party has championed the cause of the oppressed youth, students, women, workers, peasants, unemployed, disabled and the poor.

events.title: Mount Elgon insurgency
events.summary: The Mount Elgon insurgency was a conflict that started in 2005 when the Sabaot Land Defence Force militia revolted in the Mount Elgon area, Western Kenya.

events.title: National Rainbow Coalition – Kenya is founded
events.summary: The People's Liberation Party (PLP), previously known as the National Rainbow Coalition–Kenya (NARC–Kenya) until February 2025, is a political party in Kenya.

events.title: Orange Democratic Movement
events.summary: The Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) is a centre-left political party in Kenya. It is the successor of a grassroots people's movement that was formed during the 2005 Kenyan constitutional referendum campaign.

events.title: Sauti Sol is formed
events.summary: Sauti Sol is a Kenyan afropop band formed in Nairobi in 2005 by vocalists Bien-Aimé Baraza, Willis Chimano, and Savara Mudigi. Initially an a cappella group, they later added guitarist Polycarp Otieno before adopting the name Sauti Sol.

events.title: The Gor Sunguh Commission
events.summary: The Gor Sungu Commission was a Kenya Parliamentary Select Committee investigating circumstances leading to the death of the late Dr. Robert Ouko.

events.title: Kenyan constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Kenya on 21 November 2005. Although many government officials, including President Mwai Kibaki, had campaigned for a "yes" vote, the proposed new constitution was rejected by 58% of voters.

events.title: 2006–2007 East Africa Rift Valley fever outbreak
events.summary: East Africa had a regional outbreak of Rift Valley fever in late 2006 that affected Kenya, Somalia, and Tanzania. During outbreak, 1062 people were infected with Rift Valley fever and 394 people died between December 2006 and December 2007.
events.source_name: Wikipedia: 2006–2007 East Africa Rift Valley fever outbreak

events.title: Kiruki Commission
events.summary: The Kiruki Commission was a Kenyan government commission established to inquire into the scandal of two alleged Armenians widely believed to be con men with high-level connections who briefly commanded attention on the streets of Nairobi in 2006.

events.title: Olare Orok Conservancy is established
events.summary: Olare Motorogi Conservancy is a 140-square-kilometer (54-square-mile) community-based conservation area in Kenya, part of the Maasai Mara-Serengeti ecosystem and wildlife dispersal zone. It borders the Maasai Mara National Reserve.

events.title: Sexual Offences Act 2006
events.summary: The Sexual Offences Act, Act No. 3 of 2006, is an Act of the Parliament of Kenya that creates a range of sexual offences.

events.title: Wiper Democratic Movement
events.summary: The Wiper Patriotic Front (WPF), until 2025 known as the Wiper Democratic Movement–Kenya (WDM), and originally called the Orange Democratic Movement–Kenya (ODM–Kenya), is a political party in Kenya, which originated as a result of the 2005 Kenyan constitutional referendum. The party tends to be more popular among the Kamba people.

events.title: President Mwai Kibaki has declared the ongoing drought a national disaster and appeal for US$150 million to feed the hungry
events.summary: President Mwai Kibaki has declared the ongoing drought a national disaster and appeal for US$150 million to feed the hungry. The lack of rains over the last three years has left 2.5 million people close to starvation.

events.title: A five-story building in Nairobi collapses and kills at least eight people, burying dozens more
events.summary: A five-story building in Nairobi collapses and kills at least eight people, burying dozens more. Rescuers use their bare hands to dig through the rubble.

events.title: In a televised address to the nation, Kenyan President Mwai Kibaki announces the resignations of two government ministers in connection…
events.summary: In a televised address to the nation, Kenyan President Mwai Kibaki announces the resignations of two government ministers in connection with two separate corruption scandals, the "Goldenberg" and "Anglo Leasing" affairs. Energy minister Kiraitu Murungi and education minister George Saitoti both deny any wrongdoing.

events.title: Kenyan police instruct 20 leading figures not to leave the country as investigations into two corruption scandals, the Goldenberg and…
events.summary: Kenyan police instruct 20 leading figures not to leave the country as investigations into two corruption scandals, the Goldenberg and Anglo Leasing scandals continue. Among the people told to hand in their passports is George Saitoti whose resignation as education minister was announced by President Mwai Kibaki yesterday.

events.title: Oxfam reports hundreds of thousands are affected by severe water shortages in Kenya and Somalia
events.summary: Oxfam reports hundreds of thousands are affected by severe water shortages in Kenya and Somalia.

events.title: Kenya and Sudan, completing trade talks that have gone on since 2001, announce plans to sign a landmark trade agreement
events.summary: Kenya and Sudan, completing trade talks that have gone on since 2001, announce plans to sign a landmark trade agreement. Kenya, which is currently in a drought, is in desperate need of food to feed 3.5 million Kenyans by the end of March, despite the presence of the U.N. food agency.

events.title: Six people have been charged in connection with Kenya's biggest fraud, which cost the government about $600m
events.summary: Six people have been charged in connection with Kenya's biggest fraud, which cost the government about $600m.

events.title: 2006 Kenyan Air Force Harbin Y-12 crash
events.summary: On 10 April 2006, a Kenya Air Force Harbin Y-12 II operating as Flight I-32, flying from Nairobi to Marsabit, Kenya, crashed into Mount Marsabit in bad weather as it was approaching Marsabit airstrip a second time after aborting its first attempt, killing 14 of the 17 occupants on board, including a number of politicians. The flight to the region was carrying a peace delegation meant to mediate regional feuds, which were exacerbated by a food crisis.
events.source_name: Wikipedia: 2006 Kenyan Air Force Harbin Y-12 crash

events.title: 2006 Kenya plane crash, 14 people and a number of politicians are killed in a plane crash near Marsabit
events.summary: 2006 Kenya plane crash, 14 people and a number of politicians are killed in a plane crash near Marsabit.

events.title: Evangelist Gilbert Deya is arrested by police at Edinburgh Sheriff Court in relation to allegations by Kenyan police of involvement in…
events.summary: Evangelist Gilbert Deya is arrested by police at Edinburgh Sheriff Court in relation to allegations by Kenyan police of involvement in child trafficking.

events.title: A couple is caught having sex in a mosque during Ramadan in Gilgil and are sentenced to 18 months in prison
events.summary: A couple is caught having sex in a mosque during Ramadan in Gilgil and are sentenced to 18 months in prison.

events.title: 2006 United Nations Climate Change Conference
events.summary: The 2006 United Nations Climate Change Conference took place between November 6 and 17, 2006 in Nairobi, Kenya. The conference included the 12th Conference of the Parties to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) (COP12) and the second Meeting of the Parties to the Kyoto Protocol (MOP2).
events.source_name: Wikipedia: 2006 United Nations Climate Change Conference

events.title: Chuka University is founded
events.summary: Chuka University is a public university in Kenya.

events.title: Dedan Kimathi University of Technology is founded
events.summary: Dedan Kimathi University of Technology (or DeKUT) is a public university in Nyeri, Kenya.
events.source_name: Wikipedia: Dedan Kimathi University of Technology

events.title: Kenyan tea workers strike of 2007
events.summary: The Kenyan tea workers strike of 2007 was a strike action undertaken by members of the Kenya Plantation and Agricultural Workers Union (KPAWU) against Unilever Tea Kenya Ltd (UTK) over a wage increase. It took place in the Kericho region of Kenya and involved an estimated 10,000 workers from eighteen tea plantations.
events.source_name: Wikipedia: Kenyan tea workers strike of 2007

events.title: Kenya tightens security at Somalian border in order to prevent Islamic Courts Union militants from entering Kenya [1]
events.summary: Kenya tightens security at Somalian border in order to prevent Islamic Courts Union militants from entering Kenya [1].

events.title: Murfy's fLaw
events.summary: Murfy's fLaw is a Kenyan alternative rock band formed in Nairobi, Kenya, in 2007.

events.title: Nairobi International Convention on the Removal of Wrecks
events.summary: The Nairobi International Convention on the Removal of Wrecks is a 2007 treaty of the International Maritime Organization (IMO). The purpose of the convention is to establish uniform rules for the prompt and effective removal of shipwrecks located in the exclusive economic zone (EEZ) of a state that may be hazardous to navigation or to the environment.
events.source_name: Wikipedia: Nairobi International Convention on the Removal of Wrecks

events.title: Party of National Unity is founded
events.summary: The Party of National Unity (PNU) is a political party in Kenya originally founded as a political coalition. On 16 September 2007, Kenyan President Mwai Kibaki announced the party's formation and declared that he would run as its presidential candidate in the December 2007 Kenyan elections.

events.title: Pwani University is founded
events.summary: Pwani University is a public university in the Kilifi County in the coastal region of Kenya, located 60 km north of Mombasa in the resort town of Kilifi, within the larger Kilifi County. Prior to the award of a charter, the university was a constituent college of Kenyatta University.

events.title: Waki Commission
events.summary: The Waki Commission, officially The Commission of Inquiry on Post Election Violence (CIPEV), was an international commission of inquiry established by the Government of Kenya in February 2008 to investigate the clashes in Kenya following the disputed Kenyan presidential election of 2007.

events.title: Three Administration Police officers shot dead near Molo, Nakuru District
events.summary: Three Administration Police officers shot dead near Molo, Nakuru District. On January 7 two suspects were shot down by police in Elburgon, Nakuru District.

events.title: Rift Valley Fever outbreak in northeastern Kenya has reached a death toll of 95, out of 248 reported cases
events.summary: Rift Valley Fever outbreak in northeastern Kenya has reached a death toll of 95, out of 248 reported cases. Most affected are Garissa, Wajir, Ijara and Tana River districts.

events.title: Kiraitu Murungi and David Mwiraria were cleared from allegations of being involved with the Anglo-Leasing scandal
events.summary: Kiraitu Murungi and David Mwiraria were cleared from allegations of being involved with the Anglo-Leasing scandal.

events.title: 25 – World Social Forum meeting held in Nairobi
events.summary: 25 – World Social Forum meeting held in Nairobi.

events.title: A recording of a conversation involving David Mwiraria recorded on 11 June 2004 is released by John Githongo
events.summary: A recording of a conversation involving David Mwiraria recorded on 11 June 2004 is released by John Githongo. According to the tape, Mwiraria tried to stop investigations on the Anglo-Leasing scandal, in which he was a suspect.

events.title: Ban Ki-moon, the new Secretary General of United Nations visits Kenya
events.summary: Ban Ki-moon, the new Secretary General of United Nations visits Kenya.

events.title: The statue of Dedan Kimathi was unveiled in Nairobi
events.summary: The statue of Dedan Kimathi was unveiled in Nairobi. The date coincided with the 50th anniversary of his execution by colonial administration.

events.title: Simon Matheri Ikere, the most wanted criminal as declared by Kenya Police, is shot by the police after they surrounded him, having been…
events.summary: Simon Matheri Ikere, the most wanted criminal as declared by Kenya Police, is shot by the police after they surrounded him, having been located through tracing of his mobile phone.

events.title: the 2006 Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education results were published
events.summary: the 2006 Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education results were published. Starehe Boys Centre was ranked the best high school in Kenya, followed by Strathmore School and Alliance High School.

events.title: Five dangerous criminals escaped Nakuru GK Prison
events.summary: Five dangerous criminals escaped Nakuru GK Prison.

events.title: Internal Security minister John Michuki proposes new tough laws against possession of illegal firearms
events.summary: Internal Security minister John Michuki proposes new tough laws against possession of illegal firearms. Similarly, the police was given a tight shoot-to-kill directive.

events.title: President Mwai Kibaki proposes constitutional reforms to be implemented before general elections set to be held in December 2007
events.summary: President Mwai Kibaki proposes constitutional reforms to be implemented before general elections set to be held in December 2007. Especially opposition members have demanded new constitutional reforms.

events.title: Tribal clashes in Mount Elgon District continue as four shops were burnt in Makutano trading centre
events.summary: Tribal clashes in Mount Elgon District continue as four shops were burnt in Makutano trading centre.

events.title: A policeman is shot dead by Mungiki sect in Kiambu District
events.summary: A policeman is shot dead by Mungiki sect in Kiambu District.

events.title: During his labour day speech, President Mwai Kibaki promises to scrap tuition fees issued by public high schools
events.summary: During his labour day speech, President Mwai Kibaki promises to scrap tuition fees issued by public high schools.

events.title: Ethnic violence in Mt
events.summary: Ethnic violence in Mt. Elgon area continues, ten people were shot dead in Kitale.

events.title: Kenya Airways Flight 507 crashes
events.summary: Kenya Airways Flight 507 was a scheduled international passenger service between Abidjan, Ivory Coast, and Nairobi, Kenya, with a stopover in Douala, Cameroon, operated by Kenya Airways. On 5 May 2007, the Boeing 737-800 aircraft serving the flight crashed immediately after takeoff from Douala International Airport in Cameroon, killing all 114 occupants onboard.

events.title: Kenya Airways Flight 507 crashes in Cameroon shortly after take-off
events.summary: Kenya Airways Flight 507 crashes in Cameroon shortly after take-off. All 114 on board perished.

events.title: By-election held in Magarini constituency was won by Harrison Garama Kombe of Shirikisho Party
events.summary: By-election held in Magarini constituency was won by Harrison Garama Kombe of Shirikisho Party.

events.title: Three wildlife rangers and four suspected poachers were shot dead during a gunfight in Tana River District
events.summary: Three wildlife rangers and four suspected poachers were shot dead during a gunfight in Tana River District.

events.title: Kenyan economy grew by 6.1 per cent in 2006, according to the government
events.summary: Kenyan economy grew by 6.1 per cent in 2006, according to the government. It is the highest growth rate in Kenya in three decades.

events.title: Over 30 suspected Mungiki members have been killed by the police within a week, following recent violence by the sect
events.summary: Over 30 suspected Mungiki members have been killed by the police within a week, following recent violence by the sect.

events.title: Eleven people were killed around Nairobi
events.summary: Eleven people were killed around Nairobi. These killings happened after John Kamunya (aka Maina Njenga), a former Mungiki leader was jailed for five years.

events.title: Eight Kenyan cattle raiders have been killed by the Uganda People's Defence Force
events.summary: Eight Kenyan cattle raiders have been killed by the Uganda People's Defence Force.

events.title: Five people were shot dead by criminals in Stony Athi, Machakos District
events.summary: Five people were shot dead by criminals in Stony Athi, Machakos District.

events.title: Earth tremors have been felt in Nairobi and elsewhere Kenya during few past days
events.summary: Earth tremors have been felt in Nairobi and elsewhere Kenya during few past days. The tremors were related to the activity of Ol Doinyo Lengai volcano in Tanzania.

events.title: Charity Ngilu, the minister of health, was arrested for several hours in Nairobi
events.summary: Charity Ngilu, the minister of health, was arrested for several hours in Nairobi. This happened after Ngilu allegedly freed Anne Njogu, a detained human rights activist.

events.title: Several people die following mudslides near Malava, western Kenya
events.summary: Several people die following mudslides near Malava, western Kenya.

events.title: 20 people die in a road accident near Yala town as a bus and petrol tanker collide
events.summary: 20 people die in a road accident near Yala town as a bus and petrol tanker collide.

events.title: The Guardian newspaper featured on its front page a story about corruption by the family of the former Kenyan president Daniel arap Moi
events.summary: The Guardian newspaper featured on its front page a story about corruption by the family of the former Kenyan president Daniel arap Moi. They claim their source of the information was WikiLeaks.

events.title: Kalonzo Musyoka and Raila Odinga were selected as presidential candidates by their respective ODM fractions, having split into two in August
events.summary: Kalonzo Musyoka and Raila Odinga were selected as presidential candidates by their respective ODM fractions, having split into two in August. Meanwhile, former president Daniel arap Moi has declared his support for president Mwai Kibaki's bid to win second term.

events.title: 14 – Ten thousand tea plantation workers undertook strike action against Unilever Tea Kenya Ltd in Kericho region
events.summary: 14 – Ten thousand tea plantation workers undertook strike action against Unilever Tea Kenya Ltd in Kericho region.

events.title: Twelve people were killed when a bus plunged into River Sio in Matayos, near Busia town
events.summary: Twelve people were killed when a bus plunged into River Sio in Matayos, near Busia town.

events.title: John Njue, the newly appointed Archbishop of Nairobi, is now elevated to cardinal status
events.summary: John Njue, the newly appointed Archbishop of Nairobi, is now elevated to cardinal status. He became the second Kenyan cardinal, the other was Maurice Michael Otunga, who died in 2003.

events.title: Main political parties (ODM, ODM-K and PNU) held their primary elections selecting parliamentary and civic candidates for the upcoming…
events.summary: Main political parties (ODM, ODM-K and PNU) held their primary elections selecting parliamentary and civic candidates for the upcoming general elections. These primaries were marred by irregularities and violence.

events.title: Solomon Nyanjui, the missing KWS helicopter pilot was found alive with minor injuries, after being missing for eight days
events.summary: Solomon Nyanjui, the missing KWS helicopter pilot was found alive with minor injuries, after being missing for eight days. The helicopter he was flying had crashed on the flanks of Mount Kenya, near Chuka town.

events.title: 2007–08 Kenyan crisis
events.summary: The 2007–2008 Kenyan crisis was a violent political, economic, and humanitarian crisis in Kenya. The crisis erupted after incumbent President Mwai Kibaki was declared the winner of the 2007 presidential election.

events.title: 2007 Kenyan general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Kenya on 27 December 2007. Voters elected the President and members of the National Assembly.

events.title: 2008–2009 Kenya drought
events.summary: Between 2008 and early 2010, Kenya, one of the countries of Eastern Africa, was affected by a severe drought, which put ten million people at risk of hunger and caused a large number of deaths to livestock in Kenyan Arid and Semi-Arid Lands (ASALs), constituting around 88% of the country. The areas which experienced the worst effects were Northern Kenya, Somalia and Southern Ethiopia, most severely in Kajiado and Laikipia.

events.title: Grand Regency Scandal
events.summary: Erupting in June 2008, the Grand Regency Scandal concerned the sale of the Grand Regency Hotel in Downtown Nairobi, Kenya, from the Central Bank of Kenya to an unspecified group of Libyan investors called "Libya Arab African Investment Company". The sale was directed by Finance Minister Amos Kimunya, leading to the passage of a near-unanimous censure of Kimunya by the Kenyan Parliament on 1 July 2008.

events.title: Kenya Vision 2030 is launched
events.summary: Kenya Vision 2030 (Swahili: Ruwaza ya Kenya 2030) is a Kenyan development program, aiming to raise the average standard of living in Kenya to middle income by 2030. It was launched on 10 June 2008 by President Mwai Kibaki.

events.title: Meru University of Science and Technology is founded
events.summary: Meru University of Science and Technology (or MUST) is a public university in Tigania West Constituency Meru, Kenya. It is in Meru County, 15 kilometres northeast of Meru Town, along the Meru-Makutano-Maua Highway.
events.source_name: Wikipedia: Meru University of Science and Technology

events.title: National Accord and Reconciliation Act 2008
events.summary: The National Accord and Reconciliation Act of 2008 is an act of the National Assembly of Kenya that temporarily re-established the offices of Prime Minister of Kenya, along with the creation of two deputy prime ministers. This act followed the February 28, 2008, power-sharing agreement between current President Mwai Kibaki and opposition leader Raila Odinga, who became the first prime minister of Kenya since 1964, when the constitution of the newly created Republic abolished the office.
events.source_name: Wikipedia: National Accord and Reconciliation Act 2008

events.title: National Vision Party is founded
events.summary: The National Vision Party of Kenya is a political party founded, by former cabinet Minister Nicholas Biwott in 2008, in the fall out of his failed attempts to seize control of former ruling party the Kenya African National Union from Uhuru Kenyatta. In December 2012, the party entered a four party coalition including the New Ford Kenya, United Democratic Movement and Kenya African National Union to field a single presidential candidate at the 2013 general elections.

events.title: Riots in Kenya escalated following the tension after disputed presidential elections
events.summary: Riots in Kenya escalated following the tension after disputed presidential elections. On January 1, 2008, a mob attacked and set fire to a church in the town of Eldoret, where hundreds of people had taken refuge.

events.title: The 10th Parliament opens
events.summary: The 10th Parliament of Kenya saw the National Assembly opened on 15 January 2008. This following the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) of Raila Odinga winning a majority in the 2007 parliamentary elections.

events.title: President Mwai Kibaki and his rival Raila Odinga met for the first time since the elections
events.summary: President Mwai Kibaki and his rival Raila Odinga met for the first time since the elections. Kofi Annan, former United Nations Secretary-General was also present.

events.title: The Government of National Unity is formed
events.summary: The Government of National Unity, also known as the "grand coalition cabinet," was a designation for the coalition government in Kenya from April 2008 to April 2013. It was formed through negotiations between the Orange Democratic Movement's leader and presidential candidate Raila Odinga and Party of National Unity's leader and incumbent presidential candidate Mwai Kibaki in the aftermath of the 2007–2008 Kenyan crisis which had followed the controversial 2007 presidential election.

events.title: The new coalition cabinet is finally unveiled
events.summary: The new coalition cabinet is finally unveiled.

events.title: Four people, including politicians Kipkalya Kones and Lorna Laboso were killed in an aviation accident
events.summary: Four people, including politicians Kipkalya Kones and Lorna Laboso were killed in an aviation accident. They were on board of a Cessna 210 plane that crashed, without survivors.

events.title: The first parliamentary by-elections in Kenya after the chaotic 2007 general elections were held
events.summary: The first parliamentary by-elections in Kenya after the chaotic 2007 general elections were held. Out of five seats contested, ODM won three and PNU two.

events.title: Amos Kimunya resigns from his post of Minister of Finance due to the Grand Regency Scandal
events.summary: Amos Kimunya resigns from his post of Minister of Finance due to the Grand Regency Scandal.

events.title: Prime minister Raila Odinga issued an order for "illegal" settlers of Mau Forest to be evicted
events.summary: Prime minister Raila Odinga issued an order for "illegal" settlers of Mau Forest to be evicted.

events.title: Cattle raiders shot around 30 herdsmen at Suguta Valley
events.summary: Cattle raiders shot around 30 herdsmen at Suguta Valley. The herdsmen were chasing raiders, who had earlier stolen their cattle, but the herdsmen ran out of ammunition.

events.title: The results of Kamukunji Constituency of the 2007 parliamentary elections were not tallied until now due to a court case
events.summary: The results of Kamukunji Constituency of the 2007 parliamentary elections were not tallied until now due to a court case. Simon Mbugua of PNU was declared the winner.

events.title: a Fokker F27-500 cargo aircraft operated by Fly540. crashed about 20 km (12 mi) from the Namber Konton airport near Mogadishu, Somalia
events.summary: a Fokker F27-500 cargo aircraft operated by Fly540. crashed about 20 km (12 mi) from the Namber Konton airport near Mogadishu, Somalia. All three crew members died.

events.title: By-elections were held in Bomet and Sotik constituencies and were won by Beatrice Kones and Joyce Laboso respectively
events.summary: By-elections were held in Bomet and Sotik constituencies and were won by Beatrice Kones and Joyce Laboso respectively. Both represent ODM, as did their predecessors, who died in an aviation accident in June.

events.title: MV Faina, a Ukrainian ship was seized by Somali pirates off the Somalian coast
events.summary: MV Faina, a Ukrainian ship was seized by Somali pirates off the Somalian coast. The ship was carrying 33 Russian T-72 tanks destined to Kenya.

events.title: The post-election violence report by Waki Commission was released
events.summary: The post-election violence report by Waki Commission was released.

events.title: A Nakumatt Supermarket and other fully operational properties were demolished in Nairobi to pave way for the expansion of Thika Road
events.summary: A Nakumatt Supermarket and other fully operational properties were demolished in Nairobi to pave way for the expansion of Thika Road.

events.title: The Kenya people celebrated the election of Barack Obama as president of the United States
events.summary: The Kenya people celebrated the election of Barack Obama as president of the United States. The following day November 6 is declared a public holiday in Kenya.

events.title: Kenyan parliament passes the Kenya Communications (Amendment) Act regulating media in Kenya
events.summary: Kenyan parliament passes the Kenya Communications (Amendment) Act regulating media in Kenya. Critics say the bill meant to suppress the freedom of press, while the Kenyan government denies it.

events.title: Joel Onyancha of Ford-People lost the Bomachoge Constituency parliamentary seat after the 2007 results were nullified due to irregularities
events.summary: Joel Onyancha of Ford-People lost the Bomachoge Constituency parliamentary seat after the 2007 results were nullified due to irregularities.

events.title: President Kibaki signs a bill disbanding the Electoral Commission of Kenya
events.summary: President Kibaki signs a bill disbanding the Electoral Commission of Kenya. It will be replaced by Interim Independent Electoral Commission (IIEC).

events.title: Over 120 political parties, four with a parliamentary representation, failed to meet the deadline for complying with the new Political…
events.summary: Over 120 political parties, four with a parliamentary representation, failed to meet the deadline for complying with the new Political Parties Act and face deregistration.

events.title: 2009 Kenyan Maize Scandal
events.summary: This was a scandal in Kenya that became public in January 2009, over the sale of imported maize. In late 2008, the ban on importation of maize was lifted by the government to allow capable businessmen to import maize to supplement the local produce that was short of the minimum required to satisfy the local market.

events.title: 2009 Kenya sex strike
events.summary: A sex strike, a form of nonviolent protest, was held by Kenyan female activists in 2009 to end the deteriorating relationship between the country's President, Mwai Kibaki, and Prime Minister, Raila Odinga, who agreed to share leadership powers in Kenya. There was a seven-day sex strike, which involved thousands of women and the wives of both the Prime Minister and President, who vowed to withhold sex from their partner.

events.title: 2009 Triton Oil Scandal
events.summary: The 2009 Triton Oil scandal involved the alleged theft of up to $47 million (USD) worth of petroleum products from the Kenya Pipeline Company by the Triton Petroleum Company. Yagnesh Devani, the CEO of Triton Oil during the scandal, fought extradition for years before returning to Kenya for trial in 2024.

events.title: Jaramogi Oginga Odinga University of Science and Technology is founded
events.summary: Jaramogi Oginga Odinga University of Science and Technology (JOOUST) is a public university in Bondo in Siaya County, Kenya. It is named after Kenya's first vice-president Jaramogi Oginga Odinga.
events.source_name: Wikipedia: Jaramogi Oginga Odinga University of Science and Technology

events.title: Kenya Communications (Amendment) Act, 2008
events.summary: The Kenya Communications (Amendment) Act, 2008 is a Kenyan Act of Parliament that was passed by the 10th Parliament of Kenya and signed into law by President Mwai Kibaki on 2 January 2009. It is a controversial amendment of the Kenya Communications Act of 1998, which authorizes the state to raid media houses and control the distribution of content.

events.title: 2009 Nakumatt supermarket fire
events.summary: The 2009 Nakumatt supermarket fire occurred when a supermarket in downtown Nairobi, Kenya, caught fire on 28 January 2009. Twenty-nine remains were located in the rubble of the destroyed Nakumatt supermarket, with police investigating a tip that security guards locked exit doors in an effort to prevent looting.

events.summary: Oscar Kamau Kingara (July 14, 1971 - March 5, 2009) was a Kenyan lawyer and human rights activist. Kingara was the founder and director of the Oscar Foundation Free Legal Aid Clinic, a human rights organization based in Nairobi.

events.title: Mathira Massacre
events.summary: The Mathira massacre was a sequence of unanticipated stonings and hackings which occurred in Karatina, Nyeri District, Central Province in Kenya on 21 April 2009. At least twenty-nine people are known to have died and three others were injured after fighting was reported between residents of the town and alleged members of the illegal Mungiki sect, described as Kenya's version of tribal sects.
